nodes.description: Mice heterozygous for deletion of the TRPS1 GATA domain show facial anomalies resembling the human syndrome and develop kyphoscoliosis and cortical and trabecular bone deficits, suggesting a generalised bone dysplasia beyond the hands and hips.

evidence.reference_title: Deletion of the GATA domain of TRPS1 causes an absence of facial hair and provides new insights into the bone disorder in inherited tricho-rhino-phalangeal syndromes.
evidence.snippet: Here we report that heterozygous mice with deletions of the TRPS1 GATA domain (TRPS1(+/Deltagt)) display facial anomalies that overlap with findings for TRPS, whereas TRPS1(Deltagt/Deltagt) mice additionally reveal a complete absence of vibrissae.

evidence.reference_title: Deletion of the GATA domain of TRPS1 causes an absence of facial hair and provides new insights into the bone disorder in inherited tricho-rhino-phalangeal syndromes.
evidence.snippet: These findings directly implicate the GATA type zinc finger of TRPS1 in regulation of bone and hair development and suggest that skeletal abnormalities emphasized in descriptions of TRPS are only the extreme manifestations of a generalized bone dysplasia.

nodes.description: TRPS1 regulates dentin mineralisation in odontoblasts. Patients have supernumerary and impacted teeth, and one patient with a missense variant had large pulp spaces suggesting impaired dentin mineralisation, together with microdontia and a missing premolar.

evidence.reference_title: Transcriptional repression and developmental functions of the atypical vertebrate GATA protein TRPS1.
evidence.snippet: TRPS1 is a nuclear protein that binds GATA sequences but fails to transactivate a GATA-dependent reporter. Instead, TRPS1 potently and specifically represses transcriptional activation mediated by other GATA factors.

nodes.description: Heterozygotes show facial anomalies, kyphoscoliosis and bone deficits; homozygotes lack vibrissae and die of neonatal respiratory failure. Growth plates show delayed chondrocyte differentiation with accelerated perichondrial mineralisation, rescued by Runx2 heterozygosity.
A viable hypomorph that reproduces postnatal growth retardation and hip dysplasia, avoiding the early lethality of knockouts.

In Trps1 mutant growth plates, chondrocyte differentiation is delayed while the perichondrium mineralises early, with increased Runx2 and Ihh signalling and expanded PTHrP expression that enlarges the proliferative zone. Halving Runx2 dosage rescues the growth-plate phenotype. This dysregulated endochondral ossification is the proposed basis of the cone-shaped epiphyses, short phalanges and metacarpals, short stature and hip malformation.
